content:
alice: Heads up — we're seeing a perf regression in prod after yesterday's scheduler tweak. 99th p95/p99 for medium sequences (512-1024) up ~18% on the optimus pools.
ben: Yikes. Any specific symptoms? overall QPS lower?
alice: QPS steady. Tail latency and kernel switch rate both increased. KV warmups spike in traces. attaching short pprof excerpt from a 5m window: 
pprof-bot: ```
flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%   function
0.70s 10.0% 10.0%      2.10s 30.0%  runtime.scheduleOne
0.50s  7.1% 17.1%      1.80s 25.7%  runtime.startKernelPath
0.45s  6.4% 23.6%      1.20s 17.1%  kernel.switchAndLaunch
0.35s  5.0% 28.6%      0.90s 12.8%  kvcache.warmup
```
carla: That startKernelPath + switchAndLaunch combo looks like increased path churn. Did the new scheduler lower stickiness thresholds?
dmitri: I bumped the scheduler hysteresis to 0.05 -> 0.02 to reduce queuing in bursts. Could definitely make kernel picks flip more often for medium sequences.
alice: Good catch. The regression correlates with deploy at 22:03 UTC yesterday which included that change.
ben: Can we reproduce in staging with traffic that has the same seqlen histogram? Our default staging uses short seqs, won't hit this.
carla: I replayed a sampled production trace to staging last night and saw identical kernel-flapping. Patch for test below.
carla: ```bash
# replay script snippet
python replay.py --trace /tmp/prod_sample.json --rps 120 --target staging
```
ben: Nice. While replaying I noticed KV warmup rate goes +40% per request because cached prefixes invalidated after kernel switch. So cost rises and latencies spike.
dmitri: Two hypotheses: 1) lowering hysteresis increased kernel switching for borderline seqlen buckets; 2) continuous-batching window changed and now launch overhead dominates for med sequences.
alice: Proposed experiments: A) revert hysteresis to 0.05 for canary pools; B) add seqlen-weighted sticky assignment in selector; C) increase batching window by 5ms to give continuous batching more fill.
ben: I can run A quickly. Revert on one pool and monitor p99 across 30m.
carla: For B, prototype algorithm: prefer last-used kernel if seqlen delta < 10% and requeue instead of switch. Pseudocode: 
pprof-bot: ```
if abs(current_seqlen - last_kernel_seqlen) / last_kernel_seqlen < 0.1:
  keep_kernel = true
else:
  evaluate_kernel_costs()
```
carla: That reduces KV churn by favoring path stability for borderline cases.
dmitri: Caution: too much stickiness hurts longseq throughput because of misrouted kernels. We need an autoscaling knob that considers both seqlen histogram and backlog.
alice: Agree. For short-term rollbacks let's do A + monitoring. For mid-term, implement B behind a feature flag + metric: kernel_stick_rate and kv_invalidate_count.
ben: Rolling revert on pool-4 now. deploy-bot: revert scheduler hysteresis on pool-4 started (run id r-2026-0318-01).
ben: pool-4 p99 back down ~12% within 6 minutes. Not fully recovered but trending.
carla: Good signal. I'll instrument kernel selector to emit sequence_len_bucket and last_kernel_id per request so we can quantify stickiness.
dmitri: Also add a sampling trace that records kernel_switch=true events with full stack to S3 for offline flamegraphing.
alice: Action items: 
- ben: finish revert rollout to all canary pools and monitor 1h window (p99, kv_invalidate_count).
- carla: add seqlen and last_kernel metrics + feature flag for seqlen-sticky heuristic.
- dmitri: run a controlled staging replay with the new hysteresis and increased batching window (5ms) to validate tradeoffs.
Everyone: please add short notes to the perf board with links to traces. :thumbsup:
